target: Exact public-domain scan of the 1920 Jastrow–Clay edition relevant to the provisional Old Babylonian Gilgamesh tradition

bibliographic_identity.title: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic, on the Basis of Recently Discovered Texts
bibliographic_identity.series: Yale Oriental Series, Researches, Volume IV, Part III

internet_archive_record.note: Internet Archive metadata supplies provenance and derivatives but no independent rights statement; Commons supplies the exact-file public-domain evidence.

bounded_findings: Jastrow is credited with the introduction, commentary, and appendix.
Clay is credited with Yale-tablet text work.
The transliteration and translation are described as joint work.

negative_and_deferred_channels.penn_images: Exact Penn CBS 07771 object metadata is useful, but the institution's custom media terms did not provide the required standard-open object license.
negative_and_deferred_channels.yale_images: YBC 2178 was exactly identified through Yale and CDLI; no exact image with a standard open license was established.
negative_and_deferred_channels.ebl_current_corpus: The eBL corpus API is open to view, while the repository MIT license applies to software rather than the corpus body.
negative_and_deferred_channels.zenodo_dataset: The eBL fragments dataset is CC BY 4.0, but a bounded exact-identifier search did not return CBS.7771 or P262784, so it was not acquired as the candidate object.
negative_and_deferred_channels.project_gutenberg: The derived HTML transcription is a useful US route but was not selected over the exact historical page scan.

snapshot_boundary: The tracked snapshot preserves identity, provenance, rights evidence, and fixity. It contains no source-bearing ancient text, OCR, transliteration, translation, semantic assertion, graph fact, canon promotion, or publication authorization.
